response:
**Short answer**

Your data is **not** deleted when a Supabase project is paused. The pause simply stops the database and disables any real‑time or authentication traffic until you resume it. All tables, rows, files, and your Supabase key values stay exactly as they were.

---

## What “paused” means

| What gets stopped | Why it matters | What stays |
|-------------------|----------------|-----------|
| **Database instance** (Postgres) | No reads or writes from your app; it won’t process SQL | All tables & rows are still there |
| **Realtime subscriptions** | No live updates are pushed | Data that could be shown when you resume |
| **Auth (signup / login)** | Your sign‑ups or magic‑link emails won’t work | Existing users, their auth data, and any profile tables |
| **Storage buckets** | No new uploads/downloads | All files you already stored |
| **Webhook triggers** | These won’t fire | All your function code remains |

When you click **Resume** in the Supabase dashboard, the instance comes back online in a few minutes. Your app can connect again with the same connection string and secrets.

---

## How to be sure

1. **Check the status.**  
   In the Supabase dashboard, the top bar will show “Paused” with an orange icon.  
   Click the **Resume** button – it turns from `▶︎` to `↩︎` when the instance is active again.

2. **Connect your app.**  
   After resuming, try a simple query (or refresh your app). If it loads rows, the data is intact.

3. **Verify storage.**  
   Go to the **Storage** tab and look at your buckets. All files should still be there.

4. **Look at the logs.**  
   In **tRPC** or **Functions**, you can view recent logs to confirm nothing was deleted.

---

## What to do if you’re worried

- **Backup your data first.**  
  Even though pause doesn’t delete data, it’s a good habit to export tables or download files.  
  • In the **Table editor**, choose **Export → CSV**.  
  • In **Storage**, click **Download** for any important files.

- **Check your quotas.**  
  Supabase free plans have limits (e.g., 500 MB DB, 1 GB storage). If you hit them, you may see “paused” automatically. Once resumed, you’ll see whether you’re still within the limit.

- **Contact Supabase Support.**  
  If you notice missing rows or buckets after resuming, reach out to support. They have logs that show exactly what happened during the pause.

---

### Bottom line

Your data is still stored safely in the paused instance. Resuming will make everything work again. If you want an extra safety net, export the tables and files now. If anything looks wrong after resuming, let me know—happy to walk you through a quick sanity‑check!
